name: Button
purpose: A button starts an action. Six variants share one size scale, one radius, and one focus ring.

variants.name: primary
variants.use: The first action. Use one primary button on each screen.

variants.name: ghost
variants.use: Toolbars, tables, and the Cancel action of a dialog footer.

variants.name: destructive
variants.use: An action that removes data. Get a confirmation first.

variants.name: link
variants.use: An action in the text, for example View all. It has no loading state.

anatomy.role: The target, the fill, and the border. The size sets its height
The action, as a verb. Example: Save
An icon at the start side or at the end side of the label
The sign of the activity of a loading button

moments.when: When the user releases the pointer on the button, or presses Enter or Space. Not at pointer down

clauses.text: The accessibility tree shows the control as a button, with the label as its name.
The label tells the action with a verb, for example Save or Mark as shipped. A control with no label that the user can see is an icon button.
Tab moves the focus to the button. Enter and Space press the button.
A button in a form does not send the form, unless its type is submit.
The size and the density set the height. Pointer: small 28 px, medium 32 px, large 40 px. Touch: small 36 px, medium 44 px, large 52 px.
A block button has the height of its size and the full width of its container.
On each axis, the target is the minimum target of the density or more. A small button in the touch density extends its target past its edges to 44 px.
The variant sets the fill, the border, and the label color. The primary and the destructive variants have the strong label weight.
A screen has one primary button.
A destructive action gets a confirmation from the user before it removes data.
Only a device with hover shows the hover state. On a phone, the button shows only the pressed state.
At pointer down, the button scales to 0.97 in 100 ms. A link button does not scale. Its opacity goes to 0.8.
Keyboard focus shows the focus ring of the language on the container: 2 px in the ring color, 2 px from the container. A pointer press shows no ring.
A disabled button has the disabled opacity and does not start its action. It stays in the focus order, and its description tells assistive technology why the action is not possible.
The screen shows the cause of a disabled button near the button.
A loading button shows a spinner, and its label changes to the activity, for example Saving. It keeps its width and the focus, and it does not start its action again.
A link button shows a loading state.
An icon has the icon size of the density and a gap of 6 px to the label. Assistive technology does not read the icon.
In a right-to-left layout, the start side is the right side. A start icon is at the right of the label.
With reduced motion, the press has no scale and the spinner does not turn. The change of color stays.
A press emits the moment press when the user releases the pointer on the button, or presses Enter or Space. A disabled or a loading button emits no moment.
The button starts a haptic or a sound directly.

On the web, put the actions at the right end, with the primary action last and 8 px between buttons. On a phone, stack the actions at full width, with the primary action first and 12 px between buttons.
